Subject: Auth operations: keys → JWT transition checklist (FinLytics)

Hi Celine —

Great to meet yesterday. Thanks again for carving out time to walk through the demo and the initial integration sketch. Per request, I wanted to capture the immediate asks and propose a minimal plan to get you from API keys to short-lived JWTs/service-account-based auth with rotation and audit hooks.

Top-line asks we captured from the call:
- Replace long-lived shared API keys for server-to-server calls with short-lived JWT tokens issued by FinLytics' identity provider (IdP) where possible.
- Maintain a fallback scoped API key for scheduled batch jobs where IdP integration is infeasible initially.
- Auditable key rotation policy (30–90 day rotation window) + an emergency revocation path.
- Guidance on embedding/reranker requests (token scoping, model routing) and how tokens should be presented for tool-calling endpoints.

Proposed immediate next steps (timeline in parentheses):
1) Technical checklist from our side (Marissa) — config snippets for Redwood SDK + example JWT exchange (1–2 business days).
2) FinLytics infra call to share IdP details & claim mappings (you and your infra lead) — schedule this week if possible.
3) We provide a fallback playbook for scoped API keys for batch pipelines + a runbook for emergency key rotation (Ben) — draft in 3 business days.
4) Joint test plan for structured output/tool-calls and embedding requests with scoped tokens (end-to-end tests) — coordinate next week.

Attachments: redwood-auth-playbook-v1.pdf (initial playbook), finlytics-integration-matrix.xlsx (integration matrix template).

Would you be up for a 30-minute call on Thursday to go over the claim mappings? If so, send a preferred time and I’ll lock it in.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz

vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0137

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying points from our infra/security team:

1) IdP + claims: We use Okta and would prefer Redwood to accept standard OAuth 2.0 client_credentials flow with JWT assertion for server-to-server. We will need example scopes so we can map them in Okta.
2) Batch jobs: The majority of our ETL runners are on a managed k8s cluster with a third-party scheduler; replacing with JWTs immediately will be a lift. The fallback scoped API key approach is acceptable if scoped to the embedding/reranker endpoints only.
3) Rotation + discovery: Can you outline how Redwood surfaces the active credential(s) in the Console and how revocation propagates to in-flight requests? We're sensitive about the time window where a revoked key might still be accepted.
4) Audit logs: We need per-token usage logs surfaced via S3 export or API (prefer S3).

We can do Thursday at 10:30am PT for the mapping call.

Also copying procurement — they asked for the contact to share the security questionnaire and a preferred format for evidence.

Best,
Celine
Head of Infrastructure | FinLytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Celine Moreau <celine.moreau@finlytics.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-07T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Auth operations: keys → JWT transition checklist (FinLytics)

Hi Celine —

Thanks — I pulled together the technical snippets and a short plan. Summary below and I attached the playbook referenced by Vanessa.

Quick answers to your bullets:
- Accepting JWTs: Redwood supports OAuth 2.0 client_credentials with JWT client assertions (RFC 7523). We'll accept tokens signed by your Okta tenant; we validate issuer, audience, exp, and a required 'redwood:scope' claim. Example scope names: 'redwood:api:embed', 'redwood:api:rerank', 'redwood:api:toolcall'.
- Fallback keys: Scoped API keys can be created with read-only or write scopes and pinned to a model/route. We recommend pinning batch jobs to a dedicated API key with a narrow scope and IP/agent restrictions.
- Revocation & propagation: We have a near-real-time revocation path — when a credential is revoked in our control-plane it is pushed to edge caches. Propagation depends on cache TTL; default TTL is 30s, but we can configure to 5s for your account during rotation windows. In-flight tokens issued by your IdP that are already validated will not be retroactively accepted after we reject the token on the next request cycle.
- Audit logs: We can export per-token usage logs to an S3 bucket on a 1-hour cadence or provide an API to pull recent events. We include token_id, route, model_id, and latency/cost metrics.

Technical snippets (embedded):
- Example JWT exchange (Okta): 
  POST /oauth/v1/token
  grant_type=client_credentials&scope=redwood:api:embed
  client_assertion_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer
  client_assertion=<signed-jwt>

- Header usage to Redwood API:
  Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
  X-Redwood-Client-Assertion: <optional-jwt-for-audit>

Runbook highlights:
1) Prepare Okta client -> register with redirectless flow, assign claim mapping to include 'redwood:scope'.
2) Create one scoped API key for batch fallback; set TTL and IP limits.
3) Schedule rolling rotation window: create new Okta client / key, update test environment, swap, and revoke old.
4) Set Console TTL to 5s for rotation events and verify revocation with a smoke test.

I'll be on the call Thursday 10:30am PT and will bring a short demo of the exchange and Console view.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
